I'm **Alfredo Ramirez Diaz**, a full-stack developer living in Massachusetts, near Boston.

I studied **Computer Engineering at UNITEC** in Honduras. My first serious work was in PHP with Yii2's MVC; later I spent years building business systems on **Frappe and ERPNext** — that's where [Ren POS](/projects), my restaurant point of sale, comes from.

Over time I kept writing the same plumbing again and again: models, forms, permissions, APIs, deployment. So I started **[Loopar](https://loopar.build)** — an open-source meta-framework where you define an entity once and get the database, the REST API, the forms and the views. This site is itself a Loopar app.

## What drives me

I'm motivated by automation and by tools that give people back their time. I also want to show other developers from Honduras, and from anywhere with fewer opportunities, that you can build serious software from wherever you start.

## Outside the code

I film planes, birds and New England landscapes under **Ardframes** — the same patience it takes to wait for the right light helps with hard bugs.

Post:Hello alfra.dev.name: Hello alfra.dev
Post:Hello alfra.dev.title: Hello, alfra.dev
Post:Hello alfra.dev.author: Alfredo Ramirez
Post:Hello alfra.dev.summary: Why this site exists, why it runs on Loopar, and what I'll be writing about.
Post:Hello alfra.dev.description:
This is the first post on **alfra.dev**, and it's a small milestone: the site you're reading is a [Loopar](https://loopar.build) app — the open-source framework I've been building.

## Why a personal site now

For a long time my work was spread across repositories, client sites and half-finished notes. I wanted one place that links it all together: the products I build, the client work running in production, and what I learn along the way.

## Why build it with Loopar

I could have used a static site generator. But dogfooding is the best test a framework can get. To publish this blog I added a generic **Post** entity to Loopar's core, so every Loopar site can now have a blog with the same collection element that already lists projects and services. If something felt clumsy while building this site, that's a bug I now get to fix.

## What I'll write about

- **Building a framework**: architecture decisions in Loopar — multi-tenancy, the designer, moving the data layer to Knex
- **Shipping to real businesses**: what restaurants, contractors and cleaning companies actually need from software
- **The path**: from Computer Engineering at UNITEC in Honduras, to PHP and ERPNext, to building my own tools in Boston

If any of that sounds useful, check back — or [say hello](/contact).

Project:BW Construction.name: BW Construction
Project:BW Construction.title: BW Construction
Project:BW Construction.summary: Company website for a construction contractor — services, reviews and lead capture.
Project:BW Construction.description:
A marketing site for a construction company, built entirely with Loopar's page builder.

* Services, reviews and contact pages managed from the desk — no developer needed for content changes
* Contact messages land in the desk as records, ready to follow up
* One of the first production sites running on Loopar, and the template I reuse for service businesses

Project:Fabulous Cleaning.name: Fabulous Cleaning
Project:Fabulous Cleaning.title: Fabulous Cleaning
Project:Fabulous Cleaning.summary: WordPress-to-Loopar migration with a server-driven cleaning quote calculator.
Project:Fabulous Cleaning.description:
Migrated a WordPress site off shared hosting and onto my own Loopar cloud — then made it more useful than the original.

* **Service calculator**: the whole configuration (counters, options, multipliers, minimum charge) is served by the server, so pricing changes never require a deploy
* The same calculator component powers the public site *and* the desk, so staff can quote a customer over the phone
* Quotes are stored as structured snapshots, editable while the lead is still open

Project:Couple Hardwood Floors.name: Couple Hardwood Floors
Project:Couple Hardwood Floors.title: Couple Hardwood Floors
Project:Couple Hardwood Floors.summary: Website and quoting engine for a hardwood flooring company in Boston.
Project:Couple Hardwood Floors.description:
Website and internal quoting tool for a hardwood flooring business.

- **Quotes built from work lines by process** — install, sand, stain, repair — where works can depend on each other, so the flow is data, not code
- Printable customer quotes with letterhead through Loopar print formats
- Project gallery and services catalog driven by Loopar's generic collections

Project:Ren POS.name: Ren POS
Project:Ren POS.title: Ren POS
Project:Ren POS.summary: Restaurant point of sale for ERPNext: floor plan, kitchen flows, reservations and payments.
Project:Ren POS.description:
A restaurant POS built as a Frappe app for **ERPNext v16**.

- Visual floor plan, table status and reservations
- Configurable kitchen flows and production stations, with a kitchen screen
- Menus, options and combos, recipes
- Roles with manager PIN, tips, split checks, card readers (Stripe Terminal) and cash register

Built with Frappe & ERPNext on the backend and React + Vite + Tailwind on the frontend.

Project:Loopar.name: Loopar
Project:Loopar.title: Loopar
Project:Loopar.summary: Open-source full-stack meta-framework: define an entity once, get database, API, forms and views.
Project:Loopar.description:
**Loopar** is the framework I wish I had when I started building business software. You define an entity — visually or in JSON — and Loopar generates the schema, the REST API, the forms, the list views and the controllers.

- **Visual designer** for entities and pages, with full code access the moment you need it
- **Single-core multi-tenancy**: many sites served by one process, each with its own database
- **Multi-database** through Knex: MySQL, PostgreSQL and SQLite
- **SSR** React + Vite + Tailwind frontend
- Batteries included: auth and owner-based permissions, email, pluggable storage (Cloudinary), analytics, an OpenAI-compatible AI layer, and a SaaS control app with Stripe subscriptions

Loopar is self-recursive — it's built with Loopar — and it's MIT licensed. This website is a Loopar app.
